parsed.attack: The call comes at a fixed time every weekday, which is the clock edge the idea's own pain paragraph warns about, and the mechanic is negatively selected by design: on days you did the thing the call is pleasant and gets answered, and on days you did not - the only days it matters - you let it ring, because declining a machine costs nothing socially, which is the first sentence of the pain statement. The ignoring starts around the third or fourth weekday, the first time the readback would name a commitment you dodged, and two declines are enough to make declining the default. The switching cost is a two-year record of promises kept and broken, which is stored inside the very thing being declined, so it defends nothing.
parsed.strongest_defence: The audience already pays real money for human check-ins, so willingness to be held to account is demonstrated rather than hoped for, and hearing three weeks of your own dodges read back is materially different from a push notification. Answer rates can be rescued by moving the call off the clock into a window the platform says the person is free, and by escalating an unanswered call to a human or a peer, which restores the social cost the bot lacks.
parsed.verdict_reason: A fixed-time call with zero social cost to decline is systematically avoided on exactly the days it would have worked, and the only repairs - a human on the other end, or an off-clock trigger - replace the product rather than defend it.
